attributes.diagnosis: cross-referenced target fnasm.py against our own build/GUNE5D/src/game/world/camera.o via powerpc-eabi-objdump -dr (real symbol names, not the <local>-redacted --clean view). Root cause isolated to the prologue: after `add r31,r4,r5` (cam = &gCameras[camIdx]) both r4 (gCameras HA/LO) and r5 (mulli camIdx*396) go dead simultaneously; target reuses r4 for `count=0`, ours reuses r5. This single divergent register-reuse choice appears to cascade through the whole-function coloring (f28/f29/f30/f31 bestYaw/nearestYaw/secondYaw/bestPitch and r6/r7/r8 loop index/offset/remaining are likewise permuted vs target throughout the for-loop body and the post-PointLineColl tail, but always with the SAME opcodes/offsets, just swapped operand registers -- confirmed via spot checks, e.g. target `fcmpo f2,f1;ble` vs ours `fcmpo f1,f3;bge` at fn+0x2a8 is the algebraically-equivalent swapped-operand form of the same compare, not a semantic difference).
